sources.title: PacLII, Cook Islands Sessional Legislation, Public Holidays Act 1999 (No. 17), as archive.org's snapshot of 29 January 2025 holds it
sources.said: "Anzac Day" shall mean the 25th day of April in each year; "Constitution Day" shall mean the 4th day of August in each year; "Cook Islands Gospel Day" shall mean the 26th day of October in each year; "The Sovereign's Birthday" shall be the same date as the reigning Sovereign's birthday is observed in New Zealand; "Christmas Day" shall mean the 25th day of December in each year; "Boxing Day" shall mean the 26th day of December in each year; "New Year's day" shall mean the 1st day of January in each year; "The Day Following New Year's day" shall mean the 2nd day of January in each year; "Good Friday" shall be the same date in each year as Good Friday is observed in New Zealand; "Easter Monday" shall be the same date in each year as Easter Monday is observed in New Zealand. ... (2) Where a public holiday (other than a Sunday and ANZAC Day) falls on a Saturday or a Sunday, the holiday shall be observed on the following Monday. If both Christmas Day, Boxing Day, New Year's day and the Day Following New Year's Day fall on a Saturday and a Sunday, then those public holidays shall be observed respectively on the next Monday and Tuesday. ... (4) If an Island Gospel day falls on a Saturday or a Sunday, Island Gospel day on that island shall be observed on the following Monday. ... sources.title: PacLII, Cook Islands Sessional Legislation, Public Holidays (Ra o te Ui Ariki) Amendment Act 2013 (No. 4), as archive.org's snapshot of 29 January 2025 holds it
sources.said: This Act amends the Public Holidays Act 1999. Interpretation Section 2 of the principal Act is amended by deleting the definition of Ra o te Ui Ariki and substituting the following- " Ra o te Ui Ariki means the first Friday of July in each calendar year".
sources.note: Saved at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-SLATE/c8b0b159-b4a5-540a-bbd6-18661cbe240c/scratchpad/dl/w16h2/ck-uiariki2013.html. The Act it amends had a definition of Ra o te Ui Ariki, so an amendment between 1999 and 2013 (not found) made the day; reading: it is a public holiday of the First Schedule as amended. Further readings: the Sovereign's Birthday is New Zealand's (the first Monday in June, as the game's New Zealand rules keep it, from the Holidays Act 2003); Anzac Day isn't moved off a weekend (2026's falls on a Saturday and stays there); any other day on a Saturday or Sunday is kept on the next day that isn't a holiday, which gives the Act's Monday and Tuesday for Christmas and Boxing Day, and New Year's two days. Not kept: each island's Gospel Day (the Second Schedule's Orders in Executive Council for Aitutaki, Penrhyn, Pukapuka, Rakahanga and Rarotonga, and any later ones, weren't read, so their days aren't known), and any amendment after 2013 (PacLII's sessional lists for 2014 to 2026 weren't read year by year). The Parliament's Gazette index for 2026 (read 2026-10-30) holds no holiday notice; its No. 13 gives employees time off to vote, not a holiday. The lists are these rules' days for 2026 and 2027.

sources.said: “Anzac Day” shall mean the 25th day of April in each year; “Constitution Day” shall mean the 4th day of August in each year; “Cook Islands Gospel Day” shall mean the 26th day of October in each year; “The Sovereign’s Birthday” shall be the same date as the reigning Sovereign’s birthday is observed in New Zealand; “Christmas Day” shall mean the 25th day of December in each year; “Boxing Day” shall mean the 26th day of December in each year; “New Year's day” shall mean the 1st day of January in each year; ... “The Day Following New Year’s day” shall mean the 2nd day of January in each year; “Good Friday” shall be the same date in each year as Good Friday is observed in New Zealand; “Easter Monday” shall be the same date in each year as Easter Monday is observed in New Zealand. ... (2) Where a public holiday (other than a Sunday and ANZAC Day) falls on a Saturday or a Sunday, the holiday shall be observed on the following Monday. If both Christmas Day, Boxing Day, New Year’s day and the Day Following New Years Day fall on a Saturday and a Sunday, then those public holidays shall be observed respectively on the next Monday and Tuesday. ... sources.note: An image-only scan, read 2026-11-03 by OCR (tesseract) and checked against the page images. Until 2026-11-03 the Act was cited to PacLII's copy (through archive.org) as primary; that copy is a legal information institute's copy of the law, so secondary since the ruling of 2026-11-03, and it was kept as the secondary it is; the Act says what it said. Read the same day in the same Library: the Public Holidays (Ra o te Ui Ariki) Amendment Act 2011, the amendment the 2013 Act implied and hadn't been found. It made Ra o te Ui Ariki (6 July) a holiday of the First Schedule from 2012, which the 2013 Act moved to the first Friday of July, and it repealed the Island Gospel Days (s. 4), the Savings (s. 5) and the Second Schedule's Orders. So each island's Gospel Day, left out because its Order wasn't read, is no holiday since 2012, which the lists already held. The Library lists no Public Holidays amendment after 2013. The 2011 Act calls its principal Act 'the Public Holidays Act 2009', which the Library doesn't hold; the amendment it makes reads on the 1999 Act's sections, so the year is read as a slip.

Island Gospel Days - Section 4 of the principal Act is repealed. 4. Savings - Section 5 of the principal Act is repealed. 5. Schedules - (1) The First Schedule to the principal Act is amended by adding the following - “Ra o te Ui Ariki” (2) The Second Schedule to the principal Act is repealed.
